{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2019–20 |team=Old Dominion Monarchs |image=Old Dominion Athletics wordmark.svg |conference=Conference USA |division= |short_conf=C-USA |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=13–19 |conf_record=9–9 |head_coach=[[Jeff Jones (basketball)|Jeff Jones]] |hc_year=7th |asst_coach1=Chris Kovensky |asst_coach2=John Richardson |asst_coach3=[[Bryant Stith]] |stadium=[[Chartway Arena]]{{efn|name=arena}} |champion= |bowl= |bowl_result= |sex=men }} {{2019–20 Conference USA men's basketball standings}} The '''2019–20 Old Dominion Monarchs men’s basketball team''' represented [[Old Dominion University]] in the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Monarchs, led by 7th-year head coach [[Jeff Jones (basketball)|Jeff Jones]], played their home games at [[Chartway Arena]]{{efn|name=arena}} in [[Norfolk, Virginia]] as members of [[Conference USA]]. ==Previous season== The [[2018–19 Old Dominion Monarchs basketball team|Monarchs]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] 26–9 overall, 13–5 in C-USA play to win the regular season championship. In the [[2019 Conference USA men's basketball tournament|C-USA tournament]], they defeated [[2018–19 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball team|Louisiana Tech]] in the quarterfinals,{{Cite news|url=https://odusports.com/news/2019/3/14/211795601.aspx|title=Ahmad Caver Makes a Fallaway 3-Pointer With 3.3 Seconds Left to Lead ODU to 57-56 Win Over Louisiana Tech|work=Old Dominion University|access-date=January 17, 2020|language=en}} [[2018–19 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]] in the semifinals,{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=401121632|title=UAB vs. Old Dominion - Game Summary - March 15, 2019|work=ESPN|access-date=January 17, 2020|language=en}} to advance to the championship game, where they faced off against [[2018–19 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]], winning the game, earning the C-USA's automatic bid into the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{Cite news|url=https://conferenceusa.com/news/2019/3/16/mens-basketball-mbb-odu-crowned-c-usa-champions.aspx?path=mbball|title=MBB: ODU Crowned C-USA Champions|work=Conference USA|access-date=January 17, 2020|language=en}} In the NCAA Tournament, they received the No. 14 seed in the South Region, where they were matched up against No. 3 seed [[2018–19 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], losing the game by a final score of 48–61.{{Cite news|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2019/03/22/purdue-basketball-stifles-old-dominion-61-48-ncaa-tournament-win/3235881002/|title=Purdue basketball perseveres to hold off Old Dominion in NCAA tournament opener|work=Journal & Courier|access-date=January 17, 2020|language=en}} == Roster == {{CBB roster/Header|year=2019|team=Old Dominion Monarchs|teamcolors=y|high_school=yes}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Jason|last=Wade|num=1|pos=G|ft=6|in=5|lbs=205|class=so|rs=|home=[[Richmond, Virginia]]|high_school=[[Trinity Episcopal School (Virginia)|Trinity Episcopal School]]}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Malik|last=Curry|num=3|pos=G|ft=6|in=1|lbs=180|class=jr|rs=|home=[[Wilmington, Delaware]]|high_school=Putnam Science Academy
